name: Macular Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Macular Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of multiple gray-white stromal opacities (maculae) scattered throughout the corneal stroma
Diffuse corneal thinning and irregularity detected on slit-lamp examination
Reduced or absent keratan sulfate in corneal tissue confirmed by immunohistochemistry or biochemical analysis
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the CHST6 gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic stromal macular opacities and corneal thinning on clinical examination, supported by keratan sulfate deficiency or CHST6 mutation confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation may be required in ambiguous cases; genetic testing aids in definitive diagnosis.

laboratory: Reduced or absent keratan sulfate in corneal tissue
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing stromal macular opacities and corneal thinning
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) revealing stromal deposits and thinning
other: Histopathology of corneal tissue showing glycosaminoglycan deposits in stroma

distinguishingFeatures: Discrete granular opacities rather than diffuse macular opacities
Presence of hyaline deposits instead of glycosaminoglycans
Amyloid lattice lines in corneal stroma
Progressive corneal opacities with branching pattern

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal opacities causing severe vision loss
Recurrent corneal erosions refractory to treatment
references: Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. IC3D Classification of Corneal Dystrophies—Edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
